lines.text: Every morning, she waves. You wave back. Not looking.
lines.say: [warm, matter-of-fact] Every morning, she waves. You wave back. [pause] Not looking.

lines.text: Forty-two.
lines.say: [quiet] Forty-two.

lines.text: So what if you knew the last time you'd see someone?
lines.say: [curious, low] So what if you knew the last time you'd see someone?

lines.text: Tonight you leave. First job. Another city.
lines.say: [dry, clipped] Tonight you leave. First job. Another city.

lines.text: Forty-two goodbyes at that door. What would you do with them?
lines.say: [warm, slower] Forty-two goodbyes at that door. What would you do with them?

lines.text: Nobody else can see it. Just you.
lines.say: [light, confiding] Nobody else can see it. Just you.

lines.text: Everyone you know has one. The times you'll meet again. In person. If your plans stay as they are.
lines.say: [plain, exact] Everyone you know has one. The times you'll meet again. In person. If your plans stay as they are.

lines.text: Calls don't count. Only being there.
lines.say: [plain, exact] Calls don't count. Only being there.

lines.text: Change your plans, and it does the maths again.
lines.say: [plain, exact] Change your plans, and it does the maths again.

lines.text: Two trips home a year. Keep that life, and the door gets forty-two more.
lines.say: [dry] Two trips home a year. Keep that life, and the door gets forty-two more.

lines.text: It's a number. It only counts down.
lines.say: [wry, offhand] It's a number. It only counts down.

lines.text: And she'll be at that door. She always is.
lines.say: [easy, certain] And she'll be at that door. She always is.

lines.text: Next morning. A new city.
lines.say: [amused] Next morning. A new city.

lines.text: The chai-wallah on platform two. One.
lines.say: [amused] The chai-wallah on platform two. One.

lines.text: One last chai, from a man you'll never see again.
lines.say: [softer] One last chai, from a man you'll never see again.

lines.text: It's the best chai of your life. Station chai.
lines.say: [surprised] It's the best chai of your life. Station chai.

lines.text: Maybe it's not just the chai.
lines.say: [curious] Maybe it's not just the chai.

lines.text: In one taste test, students were told, "This is your last chocolate."
lines.say: [quick, an aside] In one taste test, students were told, "This is your last chocolate."

lines.text: 64% picked it as their favourite. Any flavour.
lines.say: [quick, an aside] Sixty-four per cent picked it as their favourite. Any flavour.

lines.text: You almost go back for another glass. Then it wouldn't be the last.
lines.say: [amused] You almost go back for another glass. Then it wouldn't be the last.

lines.text: Metro. A total stranger. Four hundred? You'll never see her again.
lines.say: [puzzled] Metro. A total stranger. Four hundred? [dry] You'll never see her again.

lines.text: She's your commute now.
lines.say: [deadpan] She's your commute now.

lines.text: At the office, Mehta from Accounts. Three thousand.
lines.say: [dry] At the office, Mayta from Accounts. Three thousand.

lines.text: So you hide.
lines.say: [conspiratorial, quick] So you hide.

lines.text: Three thousand meetings. Most of them, actual meetings.
lines.say: [deadpan] Three thousand meetings. Most of them, actual meetings.

lines.text: First Friday. Go home, or sleep till noon?
lines.say: [teasing] First Friday. Go home, or sleep till noon?

lines.text: Home. Obviously.
lines.say: [dry] Home. Obviously.

lines.text: You thought it would drop when you left. It drops when you walk in.
lines.say: [surprised, quieter] You thought it would drop when you left. It drops when you walk in.

lines.text: This visit is already counted.
lines.say: [low] This visit is already counted.

lines.text: She's had the chai ready since your train left the city.
lines.say: [warm, fond] She's had the chai ready since your train left the city.

lines.text: Grandpa. Eight.
lines.say: [warm] Grandpa. Eight.

lines.text: And the story. The bicycle and the buffalo. You've never once stayed for the end.
lines.say: [warm] And the story. The bicycle and the buffalo. You've never once stayed for the end.

lines.text: You don't know it either.
lines.say: [pause] [dry] You don't know it either.

lines.text: You say, "Let's see. Work."
lines.say: [warm, casual] You say, "Let's see. Work."

lines.text: Thirty-nine. You didn't lose one. You lost two.
lines.say: [flat, quiet] Thirty-nine. You didn't lose one. You lost two.

lines.text: "Let's see" was a plan. And it did the maths.
lines.say: [dry] "Let's see" was a plan. And it did the maths.

lines.text: Thirty-nine. Fine. An allowance. You'll spend it carefully.
lines.say: [wry, half to yourself] Thirty-nine. Fine. An allowance. You'll spend it carefully.

lines.text: It only counts down. You've watched it.
lines.say: [certain, a little too sure] It only counts down. You've watched it.

lines.text: October. Diwali. And a deadline.
lines.say: [brisk] October. Diwaali. And a deadline.

lines.text: Thirty-nine is plenty. Skip this one. Save it for later.
lines.say: [breezy] Thirty-nine is plenty. Skip this one. Save it for later.

lines.text: Calls don't count.
lines.say: [flat] Calls don't count.

lines.text: Thirty-eight. You skipped it to save it. It's just gone.
lines.say: [low, slow] Thirty-eight. You skipped it to save it. It's just gone.

lines.text: Mehta, meanwhile, is doing fine.
lines.say: [deadpan] Mayta, meanwhile, is doing fine.

lines.text: Thirty-eight visits. A weekend each.
lines.say: [careful, slow] Thirty-eight visits. A weekend each.

lines.text: A writer, Tim Urban, did this sum. On his own guesses.
lines.say: [plain] A writer, Tim Urban, did this sum. On his own guesses.

lines.text: By the time he left school? 93%.
lines.say: [plain] By the time he left school? Ninety-three per cent.

lines.text: Of his time with his parents, in person. Used up.
lines.say: [plain] Of his time with his parents, in person. Used up.

lines.text: Your strip is thinner.
lines.say: [quiet, exact] Your strip is thinner.

lines.text: You're not at the start of your time with her. You're at the tail end.
lines.say: [hushed] You're not at the start of your time with her. You're at the tail end.

lines.text: Friday. No festival. No plan. Train, or sleep?
lines.say: [tired] Friday. No festival. No plan. Train, or sleep?

lines.text: Train.
lines.say: [quick, decided] Train.

lines.text: Thirty-eight. Here comes the drop.
lines.say: [tense, quiet] Thirty-eight. Here comes the drop.

lines.text: You open your mouth to say "Let's see".
lines.say: [quick, half-swallowed] You open your mouth to say "Let's see".

lines.text: It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.
lines.say: [hushed, slow, warm] It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.

lines.text: It only counted down because you only ever planned less.
lines.say: [warm] It only counted down because you only ever planned less.

lines.text: But then, the offer. A bigger job. A bigger city. On duty every festival.
lines.say: [brisk, tempting] But then, the offer. A bigger job. A bigger city. On duty every festival.

lines.text: Nine.
lines.say: [cold, quiet] Nine.

lines.text: The offer, or the Friday train?
lines.say: [low, warm] The offer, or the Friday train?

lines.text: Saying no isn't a plan. A ticket is.
lines.say: [dry] Saying no isn't a plan. A ticket is.

lines.text: More dal.
lines.say: [light, smiling] More dahl.

lines.text: Grandpa's story? You learned the ending. Well. You made one up.
lines.say: [amused, warm] Grandpa's story? You learned the ending. Well. You made one up.

lines.text: He prefers yours.
lines.say: [fond, deadpan] He prefers yours.

lines.text: Of course she is.
lines.say: [hushed, warm] Of course she is.

lines.text: Whose number would you want to see? Tell us below.
lines.say: [warm, plain] Whose number would you want to see? Tell us below.
